title: Pattern carries its own risk capital and asset-liability management rather than renting either
content:
Two of the three Supply Side Stablecoin Primitives that Pattern holds are switched off: the Risk Capital Rental Primitive is `Inactive` (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.2.1.1) and the Asset Liability Management Rental Primitive is `Inactive` (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.3.1.1). The Core Governance Reward Primitive is likewise `Inactive` (A.6.1.1.6.2.7.1.1.1). Only the Allocation System Primitive is live.

The existence of *rental* primitives for risk capital and ALM implies these are capacities an Agent can obtain from elsewhere in the ecosystem rather than hold itself. Pattern has not taken that route. Read together with Pattern Dev Co.'s automatic inheritance of the Primes' Total Risk Capital management requirements and its commitment to stay at or below a 90% Encumbrance Ratio (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.2.1.3.1–.3.2), the picture is an Agent that runs its own balance sheet discipline under ecosystem-level rules.

That has a direct bearing on where failure would surface. Because the risk capital obligation is not rented from a third party, a breach of it is Pattern's own breach — and it is exactly the condition the Freezer Multisig is instructed to act on.

The same reading discipline applies here as elsewhere in the Artifact: the Rental sections are fully built out with hub documents and directories, so their presence is not evidence of use. Only the `Inactive` status settles the question.
description: Both the Risk Capital Rental and Asset Liability Management Rental Primitives are Inactive, leaving Pattern Dev Co.'s inherited TRC obligations and Encumbrance Ratio commitment as the operative
